claim: Dr. Fahmy Malak was Arkansas's state medical examiner through most of Bill Clinton's governorship. Clinton and the state Crime Laboratory board declined to fire him despite more than four years of public criticism of his autopsy work, which was disputed in more than 20 deaths. Among the contested cases was one bearing on Clinton's mother, nurse-anesthetist Virginia Kelley: Malak's rulings 'included a ruling that helped Clinton's mother … avoid scrutiny in the death of a patient' (Los Angeles Times). In the 1981 death of Susan Deer, Malak attributed the death to blunt trauma from a thrown chunk of concrete and called it a homicide, a finding that shifted cause away from her medical care. A Democratic state legislator said Malak 'was sort of protected by the governor.' Clinton, Malak, and Kelley denied any connection between Malak's job security and his rulings. His role is often garbled — he was the state Medical Examiner, not a 'senator' or 'coroner.'

sources.label: Los Angeles Times — “Clinton's Ties to Controversial Medical Examiner Questioned,” James Risen and Edwin Chen, May 19, 1992.
sources.quote: his rulings included a ruling that helped Clinton's mother, a nurse-anesthetist, avoid scrutiny in the death of a patient

notes: Group B: the Malak controversy is real and contemporaneously documented (Los Angeles Times, May 19, 1992, Risen & Chen) — Clinton's years-long refusal to remove a state ME whose rulings were widely criticized, including one touching a case involving his own mother. The reel's caricature (he'd rule a shooting or strangling a 'drowning') overstates; the documented pattern is disputed rulings that critics said protected the connected, and a governor who shielded him. The Susan Deer (1981) ruling is the verified Kelley-adjacent case. The 1987 Kevin Ives / Don Henry 'train deaths' — Malak's most-cited case, later ruled homicides by a grand jury — are deliberately omitted from the claim pending this session's own primary verification; they belong here if/when chased. Primary URL is an LA Times reprint host (idfiles); the original LA Times archive is paywalled. Parked at the y2019 Clinton cluster.
